subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
subtype: Approach: thinking of how the owner must feel [Thinking]
passage: On the school bus after the field trip, Kishore's foot bumped something under the seat: a brown wallet, thick with notes. His heart jumped. Enough for the new football boots! Then he pictured Papa patting an empty pocket at the vegetable market, the worry crossing his face. "Whoever lost this is patting their pocket right now," Kishore thought. "The boots matter less than that face." He carried the wallet to Elizabeth Ma'am at the front. "I found it under my seat." She thanked him and said the office would call the owner from the cards inside.

qa.q: Where did Kishore find the wallet?
qa.a: He found it under his seat on the school bus.

qa.q: What was Kishore feeling when he pictured the owner patting an empty pocket?
qa.a: Sympathy and worry for the owner, which outweighed his wish for the boots.

qa.q: What else could Kishore do to help the owner find the wallet, and why?
qa.a: He could ask Elizabeth Ma'am how the school will let people know, so the owner can claim it.

qa.q: How might the person who lost the wallet feel when it is returned?
qa.a: Relieved and grateful, since that person had been worried about the missing money.

grounding: A boy finds a wallet on the bus, imagines the owner's worry, and decides returning it matters more than the money.

subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
subtype: Approach: thinking of how the owner must feel [Thinking]
passage: I'm Pranav, and I was sitting next to Amandeep on the evening bus when he found a brown wallet wedged in the seat. He opened it a little. There were notes inside, a bus pass and a photo of two small children. Amandeep went quiet. I said, "Finders keepers?" as a joke. He shook his head slowly. "My dad lost his wallet last month," he said. "His salary was in it. He didn't eat dinner that night. He just sat there." He looked at the photo again. "Someone's dad is going to feel like that tonight." He closed the wallet without taking anything and walked up to the conductor. I don't know exactly what he was thinking, but he didn't look back at the notes once.

qa.q: What photo was in the wallet?
qa.a: A photo of two small children.

qa.q: What might Amandeep have been feeling when he looked at the photo?
qa.a: He probably felt a pang of sympathy, remembering how upset his father was, though Pranav can't be sure.

qa.q: What else could Amandeep do to make sure the wallet reaches its owner?
qa.a: He could ask the conductor to note the bus and time, or tell a parent, so the return can be followed up.

qa.q: How might the wallet's owner feel when it comes back?
qa.a: The owner would be hugely relieved and grateful, especially if it held money needed for home.

grounding: It shows a boy finding a wallet on the bus, imagining his own father losing one, and deciding returning it matters more than the money.

subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
subtype: Approach: thinking of how the owner must feel [Thinking]
passage:
Monday: On the school bus, Akash found a black wallet under his seat. There was money inside, a lot of it. His friend Lalit whistled. Akash tucked it in his bag and said nothing.
Tuesday: At dinner his father mentioned a colleague who had lost his wallet with the month's rent in it. "He hasn't slept," Papa said. Akash put down his roti. He imagined Papa searching the house, pale. "If that were Papa," he thought, "I'd want anyone to give it back. The money doesn't matter more than him."
Wednesday: Akash took the wallet to the bus conductor and the class teacher, who found a phone number inside. The owner came to school that afternoon, almost crying with relief.

qa.q: When did Akash find the wallet?
qa.a: On Monday, on the school bus.

qa.q: How did Akash feel when Papa talked about his colleague?
qa.a: He felt uneasy and guilty, putting down his roti as he imagined his own father losing everything.

qa.q: What else could Akash have done on Monday, and why?
qa.a: He could have handed it to the conductor straight away, because the owner would have got it back a day sooner.

qa.q: How does the return look to the wallet's owner?
qa.a: The owner is overwhelmed with relief, almost crying, after days of worry.

grounding: It shows a boy who finds a wallet imagining his own father losing one, and deciding returning it matters more than the money.
